activity.notes: Qin Shi Huang, born Ying Zheng, became king of Qin before completing the conquest of the rival Warring States. In 221 BCE he unified the realm and adopted the new imperial title huangdi, becoming the First Emperor; he remained emperor until his death in 210 BCE. ATLAS reuses the existing Qin / 진나라 polity and records the 221–210 BCE imperial phase as his single representative sovereign Activity. His preceding kingship of Qin is retained as historical context rather than added as a second Activity.

sources.title: Qin Shi Huangdi 秦始皇帝
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Qin Shi Huangdi as King of the Qin State from 247–221 BCE and Emperor of the Qin dynasty from 221–210 BCE.

sources.title: Age of Empires: Exhibition Galleries
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum of Art explains that Ying Zheng unified the country under Qin rule in 221 BCE and then adopted the new title huangdi, emperor.
